Definition: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H2931); son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite:--Bartimæus.
BiblicalUsage: Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, is the blind beggar sitting by the roadside at Jericho. He cries out to Jesus, son of David, and receives his sight.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bartimaeus shows what a cry for mercy can do, because he would not be silenced by the crowd, and Jesus stood still for a blind beggar who refused to stop calling.
